exact_text: The reducer contract says: Each priority predicate includes “and no earlier priority matched,” so predicates are disjoint.

Unknown symbols, no matching synchronized row, multiple matching rows, or disagreement with persisted canonical_state rejects the transaction; SAVED means continue to the next lower-priority coordinate, not a default result.

Safety ownership remains ordered: cancellation with an active rollback is visible at priority 2; work cancellation REQUESTED, QUIESCING, CLEANING, and clean CANCELLED owns priorities 3-6; rollback owns priorities 7/7a; unresolved effects own priority 8; exact terminals own priorities 9-10; cleanup owns priority 11; active release attempt owns priority 12; subordinate release-attempt cancellation owns priority 13; release-attempt failure cleanup owns priority 14; degraded control owns priority 15; rollout owns priority 16; and the exhaustive candidate map returns at priority 17.

Priority 13 maps release_attempt_state=CANCEL_REQUESTED|QUIESCING|CLEANING|CANCELLED to SAVED. Those values cannot derive parent cancellation or terminality, because an earlier matching IX coordinate owns the parent projection and every later source is evaluated only when no earlier predicate matched.
